# violet-night

Nocturnal, technological, cinematic. A near-black blue-violet base with
deep purple surfaces and a bright but tightly contained violet accent —
used on `border_active`/`accent` only, never smeared across every
surface — plus cool off-white foreground text. More atmospheric/layered
than `monochrome` (stronger blur, lower opacities, a touch more
geometric presence) but not as dense/opaque as an industrial theme:
mood and depth over hard edges. Magenta is avoided entirely.

## Palette

| Token | Hex | Used for |
|---|---|---|
| `background` | `#0A0812` | app/window base background |
| `background_alt` | `#100D1D` | secondary background (bars, panels backdrop) |
| `surface` | `#16122A` | raised surfaces (menus, list rows) |
| `surface_alt` | `#1E1836` | secondary raised surface (hover/alt rows, tab bg) |
| `foreground` | `#E7E3F6` | body text |
| `foreground_strong` | `#F6F4FF` | headings/emphasis text |
| `muted` | `#8C84AD` | secondary/inactive text |
| `subtle` | `#463D66` | faint dividers/placeholders |
| `border_inactive` | `#342B52` | unfocused window/element borders |
| `border_active` | `#A970FF` | focused window border — the one loud color |
| `accent` | `#A970FF` | selection/highlight accent (same violet as `border_active`) |

A secondary, lighter violet (`#C6A3FF`) appears only in the wallpaper
generator and Kitty's `color12`/cursor accents as a "hot core" highlight
— it is not a `hypr.lua` color token.

## Geometry vs. monochrome

Monochrome: `border_size=1, gaps_in=8, gaps_out=16, rounding=9,
rounding_power=4, blur_size=6, blur_passes=2, active_opacity=1.0,
inactive_opacity=0.97`.

violet-night:

- `border_size = 2` (was 1) — the accent border needs to actually read.
- `gaps_in = 10`, `gaps_out = 20` (was 8/16) — a bit more breathing room,
  more immersive than monochrome's tight grid.
- `rounding = 14` (was 9), `rounding_power = 3.5` (was 4) — noticeably
  softer window shape; the slightly lower power keeps corners from going
  mushy now that the base radius is bigger.
- `blur_size = 9`, `blur_passes = 3` (was 6/2) — blur is used
  expressively here, not incidentally: it's what makes the theme read as
  "deep"/layered rather than just dark.
- `blur_noise = 0.035` (was 0.02), `blur_contrast = 1.1` (was 1.05),
  `blur_brightness = 0.82` (was 0.9) — more noise so the much stronger
  blur doesn't flatten into a gradient plate, brightness pulled down
  further so bright wallpaper glows don't wash out through the glass.
- `blur_vibrancy = 0.18`, `blur_vibrancy_darkness = 0.25` (both 0 in
  monochrome) — unlike monochrome, this theme has real color to carry
  through the blur, so a modest amount is let through instead of forcing
  a flat gray plate.
- `active_opacity = 0.94`, `inactive_opacity = 0.82` (was 1.0/0.97) —
  clearly more atmospheric/translucent, the biggest single driver of the
  "layered" feel the brief asks for, while staying well short of an
  overlay/HUD look.

Waybar/Rofi/SwayNC alpha in their `colors.css`/`colors.rasi` files were
tuned down to match (e.g. Waybar's bar background at ~0.72 alpha, Rofi's
main background at ~0.80/0xCC, SwayNC's control-center background at
~0.70) so those surfaces support the same layered depth instead of
sitting on top of it as flat panels.

## Wallpaper pack

Generated by `scripts/dev/generate_wallpaper_violet_night.py` (procedural,
stdlib-only, deterministic per-variant seed), using the shared
`Canvas`'s `radial_glow`/`blend_px` helpers for the glow work. Four
variants, all nocturnal/abstract/elegant — no neon grids, no
glitch/scanline effects, no RGB-gamer look:

- **nebula** (default/canonical `wallpapers/violet-night.png`) — soft
  overlapping blue-violet glows over quiet dark planes, one bright
  accent core, a scattering of faint far points. The most "mood" of the
  four.
- **monolith** — large dark violet architectural planes with a soft
  violet rim-light traced along one edge of each (not a hard white cut)
  — structure that reads as lit from within.
- **drift** — long soft diagonal glow bands built entirely from chained
  `radial_glow` calls, plus one bright off-center focal core. Minimal
  and atmospheric.
- **halo** — the quietest variant: mostly empty near-black-violet, one
  large soft glow off-center with two faint concentric rings. Built to
  sit behind Kitty/Rofi without competing with either.

Regenerate with:

```sh
python3 scripts/dev/generate_wallpaper_violet_night.py all wallpapers/
cp wallpapers/violet-night-nebula.png wallpapers/violet-night.png
```

## Motion

Overrides `motion.springs` only (speeds/styles use the shared defaults
in `config/hypr/animations.lua`). Every spring stays inside the
contract's 0.7-0.95 damping-ratio band — at most a faint overshoot,
never a repeating wobble — but is tuned a bit more underdamped than
monochrome's own defaults, close to (window/workspace) or a hair firmer
than (special-workspace) monochrome's own `specialWorkspaceSpring`
(ratio ~0.73), so overall motion reads as slightly more alive/cinematic:

| Spring | stiffness | damping | ratio | monochrome's ratio |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| window | 310 | 28 | ~0.80 | ~0.88 |
| workspace | 250 | 25 | ~0.79 | ~0.85 |
| layer | 330 | 31 | ~0.85 | ~0.91 |
| special_workspace | 250 | 24 | ~0.76 | ~0.73 |

## Manual verification (real hardware only)

This environment has no Hyprland/Wayland session, no `lua` interpreter,
and no Waybar/Rofi/SwayNC/Kitty binaries — only static structural/schema
checks (`tests/check_all_themes.py`, `tests/run_tests.sh`, PNG header/
size checks, JSON parsing) were run here. On a real machine:

```sh
git pull && ./apply.sh   # pick violet-night
hyprctl configerrors     # expect: clean
```

- **Windows**: open/close a few apps — the deeper blur and lower
  opacity should read as clearly more atmospheric/layered than
  monochrome's near-opaque windows, while text stays legible. The
  violet `border_active` should read as a controlled accent, not a tint
  bleeding across the whole window.
- **Motion**: window open/workspace switch/special-workspace toggle
  should all feel a touch livelier than monochrome — still no visible
  bounce/wobble, just slightly less "snapped to rest".
- **Waybar**: confirm the bar reads as dark nocturnal glass (its layer
  blur showing through at ~0.72 alpha), with the violet accent limited
  to small highlights (active workspace, etc.), not the whole bar.
- **Rofi** (`SUPER+R`): this is meant to be the strongest identity
  piece — confirm it looks distinctly "violet-night" (deep, layered,
  a clear accent on the selected row) while the list stays as legible
  as monochrome's.
- **SwayNC**: confirm the control center feels more dramatic than
  monochrome's (translucent, layered) without losing readability of
  notification text.
- **Kitty**: confirm the transparent dark-violet background looks good
  behind real terminal content and that foreground/selection colors
  stay legible at typical `background_opacity` settings.
- **Wallpaper**: `wallpapers/violet-night.png` (== `-nebula`) is the
  default — confirm it renders correctly behind Kitty/Rofi's blur, and
  that Waybar's strip and Rofi's usual position both sit over the
  deliberately-quieter zones baked into the image. Try the other three
  variants too (`monolith`, `drift`, `halo`) — copy one over
  `wallpapers/violet-night.png`, re-run `apply.sh`, no need to
  regenerate anything.
- **Hyprlock**: confirm the lock screen's blur/labels/input-field read
  clearly as this theme (violet outer/check colors) and stay legible
  over the wallpaper's default glow placement.
- **Brave**: load `themes/violet-night/brave/manifest.json` as an
  unpacked theme extension and confirm frame/toolbar/omnibox/tabs/NTP
  match the deep violet/blue-black palette, with `ntp_link` as the one
  bright violet element on the new-tab page.
